item.title: Indy 500 program visits local elementary school
item.description: Rio Grande Elementary in Terre Haute received a special visit from the 500 Festival and Indianapolis 500 Education Program, which provided students with an interactive experience to learn about the Indy 500 and its history.

item.title: ISU students bring home a national title
item.description: Indiana State University's Bailey College of Engineering and Technology's Construction Management Program won the national title at the Mechanical Contractors Association of America Student Chapter Competition, with Braidyn Hudson being named MVP presenter.

item.title: Senate passes new fentanyl bill
item.description: The Senate passed Tyler's Law unanimously, which will direct the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to provide hospitals with guidance on implementing fentanyl testing into routine ER drug screens, in an effort to prevent fentanyl poisoning tragedies.

item.title: New study shows Terre Haute housing stock is aging
item.description: According to a new study from Construction Coverage, the median age of homes in Terre Haute is 53 years old, which is 10 years older than the nation's median, and 61.6% of homes were built before 1980.

item.title: WATCH: NASA's historic Artemis II successfully lifts off, reaches orbit
item.description: Cheers erupted Wednesday at Kennedy Space Center in Florida after NASA's long-awaited Artemis II launched into the sky, embarking on its historic mission to the moon.

item.title: Agreements show how Heartland will spend millions in Sullivan County
item.description: Heartland Industrial Park has signed two agreements with the Board of Commissioners of Sullivan County to invest millions in infrastructure improvements, donate 15 acres of land, and abide by construction noise and time limitations.

item.title: Target is coming to Terre Haute
item.description: Target is coming to Terre Haute, Indiana, and will be located along the State Road 46 corridor near New Margaret Drive on the city's east side.

item.title: Mike Shimer looks back on fifty years of being a city employee
item.description: Mike Shimer has been working for the city of Robinson for 50 years, starting as a lifeguard in 1976 and eventually becoming mayor in 2023, and is looking forward to continuing to make a difference in the city.

item.title: Indiana State Police remind drivers of motorcycle safety as weather warms up
item.description: Motorcyclists are reminded to follow safety procedures, including using the four-second rule when following a motorcycle, and to wear protective gear, while drivers are reminded to increase their distance when behind a motorcycle.

item.title: Cities remind their residents of mowing ordinances
item.description: Cities in the area are reminding residents to mow their grass and keep clippings from going into the streets, as it can cause damage to the city's underground infrastructure and be dangerous for motorcycle drivers.

item.title: Indiana and Illinois senators help introduce act to increase support for veteran education
item.description: Senators Tammy Duckworth and Jim Banks introduced the Veteran Education Assistance Adjustment Act, which would increase the yearly books and supplies stipend to $1,500 and the supply stipends for apprenticeships to $128, to help veterans pursue higher education and training opportunities without being held back by rising costs.
